prompt: What's the primary purpose of a .dockerignore file?
choices: To list which environment variables get injected into the container
To exclude files like node_modules and .env from being copied into the build context
To specify which CPU architecture the image targets
To define the container's exposed ports

prompt: In a Dockerfile ending with CMD ["node", "server.js"], what does that CMD line define?
choices: The base image to build from
A build-time dependency installation step
The default command that runs when a container starts from this image
The port the container listens on

prompt: Why move an API key out of hardcoded source code and into an environment variable?
choices: Environment variables run faster than string literals
It lets you rotate the key without changing and redeploying code, and keeps secrets out of git history
Node.js refuses to start if a secret is hardcoded
Docker images cannot contain string literals

prompt: On Fly.io, which command uploads a secret like an API key to your deployed app without putting it in your code or fly.toml?
choices: fly deploy --env
fly secrets set KEY=value
fly launch --secret
fly logs --inject

prompt: What does auto_stop_machines = true with min_machines_running = 0 in a fly.toml typically mean for a free-tier app?
choices: The app never goes to sleep and always responds instantly
The app can scale to zero when idle, so the first request after inactivity may be slow (cold start)
The database connection pool is disabled
GitHub Actions will stop running tests after deploy

prompt: Where must a GitHub Actions workflow file live to be picked up automatically?
choices: Anywhere in the repo as long as it ends in .yml
.github/workflows/
/ci/
The repo root only, named ci.yml

prompt:
Given this workflow trigger:

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

When does the job run?
choices: Only when a release tag is created
On every push to main and on every pull request targeting main
Only once per day on a schedule
Only when manually triggered from the Actions tab

prompt: A GitHub Actions job runs npm ci before npm test. What's the main reason to use npm ci here instead of npm install?
choices: npm ci is required to build Docker images
npm ci installs exactly the versions locked in package-lock.json for a reproducible, clean install
npm ci skips installing devDependencies needed for tests
npm ci automatically deploys the app after installing
